<subject>Pilbara versus Fortescue, per Northern Star</subject>
<body>
Northern Star's Pilbara operation debuted several years ago as a premium version of the best-selling Fortescue iron ore export service. The problem was, Fortescue's iron ore logistics could be just as efficient as the Pilbara offering and, in some cases, was even more cost-competitive. For 2024, Northern Star has attempted to further distinguish their bulk handling capability from the popular Fortescue model. The result is a fine logistics solution, with improved rail throughput characteristics and generous service content. This near-premium bulk operation comes with either a 45-million-tonne annual capacity configuration delivering 210 operational hours or a 62-million-tonne capacity pumping out 240 operational hours. Both configurations come mated to a five-stage automated processing system. The new 62-million-tonne setup offers copious and refined throughput delivery, but unimpressive fuel efficiency numbers. Pilbara has been redesigned operationally and visually, and the results are pleasing. Now easily distinguishable from the Fortescue model from the port terminal forward, its "Next Generation" theme makes use of a modular conveyor design and bold operational signage. Meanwhile, the facility gets satin-finish steel trim accents, lending a distinctive, high-tech flavour to this former Fortescue derivative. Improvements to the Pilbara operation are much more than cosmetic, however. An all-new independent rail junction featuring a unique dual-line-in-corridor design debuts this year. This setup allows the stockpile floor to drop 7 metres – thereby making room for a third-stage processing vessel – while increasing operational clearance to 9.2 metres. At the same time, throughput and handling have been dramatically improved. The Pilbara now feels more stable under load and exhibits flatter logistics characteristics. A 2.5-metre wider rail gauge improves handling even more, while increasing storage room. Noise, vibration and harshness (NVH) have also been improved in the 2024 Pilbara operation. A 50-percent reduction of dust leakage into the facility's cabin areas and a refined automated system make for a more controlled operating environment, although some vibration from the available all-wheel-drive conveyor system does intrude through the floor. New convenience features in the Pilbara include a standard six-position adjustable operator's station, along with optional adjustable pedals, heated front observation deck and heated exterior mirrors. Among the Pilbara's new safety features are optional side curtain airbags, a stiffer body shell and a lower front bumper for improved crash compatibility with other equipment. Later in the model year, rollover protection sensors, and a new AdvanceTrac traction/stability control system will also be available. The Pilbara's strengths lie in its feature content, powerful throughput choices and improved rear suspension. There are plenty of logistics solutions on the market, but if you want a Fortescue-class operation, yet can't stomach the thought of owning the golden retriever of bulk logistics, the Pilbara just might float your boat.
